objective: Confirm current-source Chromium two-versus-three worker measurements on fresh real four-CPU hosts; a product-default change still needs lifecycle/lookup qualification.

pilot.purpose: Characterize timing, route and whole-browser memory; retain every observation. Does not qualify production change.

memory.sampling: Owned root and descendants identified by PID + process start time; sampled aggregate RSS and PSS, interval 100 ms. Import and post-completion windows kept distinct. Timing nonauthoritative.
memory.purpose: Four candidate memory pairs and two A/A controls with unchanged sampler/options; import and post-completion windows independently evaluated.

correctness: Exact source/package/module hashes, current-operation completion event, worker receipts/counts, complete dictionary table counts, unique-content counts, source byte counts, published generation, at least 12 readable source-derived probes. Complete all-row logical parity and lifecycle qualification still required before a product default change.
nextDecision: Set explicit confirmatory memory ceiling from retained pilot before any acceptance cohort. Reject worker policy if visible timing neutral/opposite-signed or memory/responsiveness cost is unacceptable. No navigator overrides or deleted samples.
limits: Focused import lanes are not full lifecycle gates.
Linux hosted evidence does not by itself qualify ARM/mobile.
RSS sum duplicates shared pages; sampled peak is not an exact physical-memory maximum.

timing.interpretation: Replicated paired source-import evidence per dictionary, retain every opposite-signed pair. Any failure or large control instability with effect inside its range remains inconclusive.
